info.name: MicroLink API (through the gateway)
info.description:
Every endpoint of the seven MicroLink services, called through the API gateway on port 8080 exactly as the mobile application calls them.

How to use:
1. Start the system: docker compose up -d
2. Open 'Start here' > 'Log in' and press Send. The token is stored automatically.
3. Every other request inherits that token, so they can be sent straight away.

Requests that need a different role (shop owner, delivery agent, administrator) just need a different log-in: change the email and password variables and send 'Log in' again.

Generated from each service's own OpenAPI document, so the paths and bodies match the running code.

exec: // Stores the token so every other request can use it.

request.description: Run this first. The token is saved as a collection variable and sent automatically by every other request.

Register a shop owner or delivery agent together with their documents.

One request, one transaction. Registering first and uploading afterwards
left applicants with an account they could not log into and no documents
attached when an upload failed -- an account nobody could use and no
admin could action. Here nothing is written unless every document is
accepted, so "no documents" simply means "no account".

Serve a document's bytes to its owner or to an admin.

Unlike shop photos this is not public -- these are identity documents.

REQ-ADMIN-3. Deleting an admin, or yourself, is refused -- it is far
too easy to lock the whole platform out by accident.
REQ-ADMIN-3: undo a deactivation.
REQ-ADMIN-1/2: what the admin reviews before approving an account.

REQ-ADMIN-1/2: turn down a shop owner or agent application, with a
reason the applicant is actually told.

query.description: Search shop names, addresses, categories and product names
true = only shops that are open now
Admin verification queue: unverified shops, newest first, ignoring other filters

request.description:
Real places from OpenStreetMap (Overpass) near a point.

These are display-only: every result carries source="openstreetmap" and an
id that does not exist in MicroLink, so the app must never treat one as a
registered shop.

SRS REQ-SEARCH-3: turn a landmark name into a point, then return the
shops inside the radius (default 2 km) of that point.

Turn a dropped map pin into a readable address.

Used by the delivery-location picker: the customer can place their
delivery point anywhere, and the agent needs an address, not a pair of
coordinates. Declared before /{shop_id} so the literal path is not read
as a shop id.

REQ-ADMIN-6: the most-searched categories.

Derived from `search_impression` events, which are recorded per shop
whenever a shop appears in a result set -- so this measures which
categories people's searches actually surface, which is the closest
honest proxy for "top searched categories" without storing raw query
strings (which would be personal data we have no reason to keep).

Public: it feeds admin analytics, but there is nothing sensitive in an
aggregate category count, and keeping it unauthenticated means
admin-service can proxy it without forwarding credentials.

request.description: REQ-SHOP-1: up to 10 photos per shop (added as links - there is no file storage).

REQ-SHOP-1: upload a real photo file (up to 10 per shop).

The bytes live in Postgres rather than object storage: this project has
no S3 bucket provisioned, and a resized JPEG is a couple of hundred KB.
Swapping to S3 later means changing this function and the serve endpoint
below -- nothing else, because the app only ever sees `url`.
Serve an uploaded photo. Public: shop photos are public content, and requiring a token here would break plain loading in the app.

query.description: Only products with this stock status

request.description:
Attach a photo to a product (shop-owner storefront).

One image per product rather than a gallery: on a phone listing, the
thumbnail is what sells the item, and asking a micro-business owner to
curate several shots per product is friction they will not accept.
Public: product photos are shop-front content, and requiring a token would stop a plain in the app from loading them.

SRS REQ-SHOP-2. Accepts the old {"is_open": bool} or a full status with
an optional reason and expected re-open time.
REQ-ADMIN-1: approve (or un-approve) a shop registration.

Vouch that an unverified shop really is there. Send the CUSTOMER's own position, not the shop's -- a confirmation from further than confirm_radius_km (5 km) away is refused. Needs a verified account whose trust score is at least 50, and an owner cannot confirm their own shop. Once community_confirmations_to_verify (3) distinct nearby customers have confirmed it AND the shop lists min_products_to_verify (5) products, it is verified with verified_via = "community" and no admin is involved. The coordinates below are Homagama.

How far a shop is towards being verified by its neighbours: confirmations, required, is_verified, verified_via, whether the caller has already confirmed, and how many products the owner still has to list. Works signed out, where confirmed_by_me is always false.

Rank nearby open shops for this user with a hybrid score blending:
content affinity (their category taste), collaborative filtering (what
like-minded users favourite), global popularity, proximity and freshness --
then re-rank for category variety. Falls back gracefully to
popularity + proximity for a brand-new user with no history.

Orders placed with a shop, for its owner -- including the pickup code
they read out to the collecting agent.

The assigned delivery agent gives an accepted order back to the pool, before they have collected it. The order returns to 'pending' for other agents rather than being cancelled, and this agent is free to accept another one. Refused once the parcel has been picked up.
The customer confirms the order reached them. Marks it delivered and releases the agent for their next job -- the alternative to the agent typing the customer's delivery code.
The shop owner confirms they handed the order to its agent -- the alternative to the agent typing the shop's pickup code.

REQ-CROWD-4: attach the optional photo to a road report.

A separate call rather than a multipart create, so the report is saved
the moment the user submits it -- a failed photo upload on a bad rural
connection must not lose the report itself.
Public: approved road reports are shown to every driver on the map.

request.description:
A shop owner (or anyone) submits an ad for a shop or an outside
company to run on the customer Home screen. Always starts pending --
only an admin can approve it (see `update_ad_status` below).

Admin sees every submission (for the moderation queue); anyone else
only sees their own submissions and their review status.

advertiser's brand before -- or instead of -- approving it as-submitted.
